          <script>
          document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
            for (const [id, chapter, seconds] of [
              ["ask-anytime", "0", 15], ["your-questions", "qa", 502]
            ]) {
              const slide = document.getElementById(id);
              slide.dataset.chapter = chapter;
              slide.dataset.seconds = seconds;
            }
            document.querySelectorAll("section[data-seconds]").forEach(slide => {
              slide.dataset.timing = slide.dataset.seconds;
            });
            const title = document.querySelector("#title-slide");
            const views = [
              ["#atlas-opening video", "Wheeled Atlas", "Boston Dynamics"],
              ["#body-fixed-arm video", "ALOHA", "Zhao et al."],
              ["#body-mobile-arm video", "Galbot G1", "Galbot"],
              ['[data-w13-photo="robotis-op3"] img', "OP3", "ROBOTIS"]
            ];
            const gallery = document.createElement("div");
            gallery.className = "w13-cover-views";
            for (const [selector, name, credit] of views) {
              const reference = document.querySelector(selector);
              if (!reference) continue;
              const figure = document.createElement("figure");
              const image = document.createElement("img");
              image.src = reference.getAttribute("poster") || reference.getAttribute("src");
              image.alt = name;
              const caption = document.createElement("figcaption");
              const label = document.createElement("strong");
              label.textContent = name;
              caption.append(label, document.createElement("br"), credit);
              figure.append(image, caption);
              gallery.append(figure);
            }
            if (gallery.childElementCount) title.querySelector("h1").after(gallery);
            // Students can pick a different panel on each pass through a four-way comparison.
            for (const clip of document.querySelectorAll(".video-card video")) {
              clip.loop = Boolean(clip.closest(".w13-film-grid"));
              const panel = clip.closest(".w13-film-panel");
              if (panel) clip.setAttribute("aria-label", panel.querySelector("p").textContent.trim());
            }
          });
          </script>

## An encoder counts marks as the wheel turns {#wheel-encoder data-chapter="1" data-seconds="90"}

A disc with **8 marks** turns with the wheel. A fixed sensor counts each mark that passes.

{{< inline-svg ../../Figures/lectures/dgist-2026f-w13/encoder-count.svg width="90%" >}}

```{=html}
<span class="fragment w13-count-run" data-fragment-index="0" aria-hidden="true"></span>
```

[**6 of 8 marks** in one second: **¾ turn per second**. The target was 1.]{.fragment fragment-index="1"}


## How far did the cart go? {#four-questions data-chapter="1" data-seconds="95"}

Both front wheels turned **¾ of a turn**. Where would you put a ruler?

{{< inline-svg ../../Figures/lectures/dgist-2026f-w13/wheel-travel-check.svg width="96%" >}}

:::: {.r-stack}
[Measure where the cart started and ended against marks on the floor.]{.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="0"}

[**Proprioception**, sensing your own body’s motion, takes more than one encoder.]{.fragment fragment-index="1"}
::::

## Which reading calls for a larger correction? {#proportional-correction data-chapter="5" data-seconds="110"}

{{< inline-svg ../../Figures/lectures/dgist-2026f-w13/angle-readings.svg width="96%" >}}

:::: {.r-stack}
[Same gain for both readings. **A or B?**]{.fragment .fade-out fragment-index="0"}

[A has **10°** left. B has **2°** left.]{.fragment .current-visible fragment-index="0"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}
[<var>u</var> = <var>K</var><sub>p</sub>(<var>r</var> − <var>y</var>)]{.w13-equation}

Correction = gain × (target − reading)
:::
::::

::: {.footnote}
[Stanford CS123 · Measuring one joint · Fall 2026](https://cs123-stanford.readthedocs.io/en/latest/schedule/labs/fall-26/lab-1.html)
:::

## What hardware contributed to robot learning this month {#why-now data-chapter="8" data-seconds="55"}

| November 2026 | What the hardware made possible |
|:--|:--|
| **Nov 2** · SO-101 arm | Replay failed stacks with the commands and joint readings. |
| **Nov 3** · G1 hands | Ask for a squeezing force as well as a hand position. |
| **Nov 9** · Atlas ankle | Tune a simulated motor to the measured response. |

::: {.footnote}
[ArmnetBench · Table 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.03168v1) · [Berkeley Ctrl-F](https://forcectrl.github.io/#hardware) · [Boston Dynamics · Atlas](https://bostondynamics.com/blog/atlas-on-a-roll/)
:::
